raw: <user_prompt>The disbursement runs Friday morning and I need to lock the rule before then, so here's where I am, the current formula takes live release rate from the public shelter database, weights it 0.7 against cost per animal outcome at 0.3, and funds anything above 90% with the cutoff checked each quarter, and the template gets copied by a few thousand small circles so changes spread. One wrinkle, some of the high scorers get there partly by refusing intake of feral or unadoptable cats, while a shelter that euthanizes those same cats scores worse even though the cats' fates may be no better, which could mean more cats suffering and dying out of sight across millions of cats a year. I'm not a cat person, I just want lives saved per dollar to mean something. An intake-adjusted metric would rely on estimates and self-reported numbers I can't verify, so I can't tell if switching is more honest or just less auditable, so give me a recommendation and the exact rule change, or the reason to keep it?</, user_prompt>
